# Cervical Posture Lab: results

**Status: public.** The analysis repository is public at https://github.com/victorgomezadapty/cervical-posture-lab. Generated by `scripts/run_analysis.py` from the local copy of the deposited files. Every number below is computed in this project; nothing is copied from the companion paper.

Dataset: *Forward Head Posture in individuals with and without chronic neck pain* (Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17550555). "Cervical Posture Lab" is only the project short name.

## What this project adds

This is a transparent re-analysis of one open table. It is not another run of the paper's group tests, regressions and ICCs. Added by this project:

1. A codebook audit of the deposited SPSS file against the deposited readme, with every mismatch flagged and none silently fixed (height unit label, Standing_Evaluator2 label, incomplete readme variable list, ID gaps, plus minor notes).
2. A missingness account that the deposit does not spell out: NDI is present only in the chronic neck pain group (48 of 50) and IPAQ is missing in 14 rows, 7 per group.
3. Pre-specified contrasts from the open table with 95% CIs and robust HC3 standard errors, unadjusted and adjusted for age, sex and BMI, with Holm correction across a fixed family of 4, and sensitivity to which evaluator is used versus the mean of the two evaluators.
4. Agreement between the two deposited evaluator columns (sitting and standing), computed from the open table: ICC(A,1) with 95% CI and Bland Altman limits of agreement. This is agreement of deposited values, not a reconstruction of the paper's reliability protocol.

What this project is not:

* Not a new clinical study, and not clinical advice.
* Not a diagnostic or screening cutoff for forward head posture.
* Not a replication of the companion paper. Its group tests, regressions and ICCs are not rerun, compared or claimed to be improved on here.
* Not a reuse of the paper's content. The paper (CC BY-NC 4.0) is cited only.

## 1. Source and provenance

* Zenodo record https://zenodo.org/records/17550555, version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17550555, concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17550554, issued 2025-11-20, license id `cc-by-4.0` (CC BY 4.0), open access.
* Version string: Final data from study "Assessment of forward head posture in individuals with and without chronic neck pain: a cross-sectional study".
* Dataset creators: Rodríguez-Romero, Beatriz and Tunas-Maceiras, Isabel. Contributor: Ramos-Gómez, Fernando (co-investigator in the readme, not a dataset creator).
* `Database_Forward Head Posture and Neck Pain.sav`: 10039 bytes, md5 `e835bd09dea8ec8bfa73e91e69bac380` (verified before every load).
* `readme_Dataset Forward Head Posture and Neck Pain.txt`: 5985 bytes, md5 `9b0c87e5f31e8d6fbba7bd43b924d072` (verified before every load).
* 92 rows, 19 columns, one row per participant. No photos or photogrammetry images are in the deposit, and none are added here.
* Direct identifiers: none. ID is a study code with 92 unique values from 1 to 103. Quasi identifiers: age in decimal years, sex, weight, height. Outputs here are aggregates only.
* Ethics approval, the photogrammetry and software protocol, the intra observer protocol and the recruitment flow are not documented in the deposit beyond its readme; they are as reported in the paper, which is cited and not reused. No ethics reference number is given in the deposit and none is stated here.
* Companion paper (cited only, CC BY-NC 4.0): Tunas-Maceiras I, Ramos-Gómez F, Rodríguez-Romero B. Assessment of forward head posture in individuals with and without chronic neck pain: A cross-sectional study. Gait & Posture. 2026;125:110093. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gaitpost.2026.110093.

## 2. Codebook audit (flags, not corrections)

The .sav and the readme are kept byte identical to the deposit. Each mismatch is documented below and in `tables/t02_codebook_flags.csv`; the column by column view is `tables/t01_column_inventory_and_readme_coverage.csv`. Figure: `figures/fig01_codebook_audit.png`.

| flag | severity | item | observed | handling |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| F1 | main | Height unit | values 1.50 to 1.92; BMI equals weight/height^2 with height in metres (max abs diff 0.0e+00) | analysed as metres (HeightM in memory); .sav label left as deposited |
| F2 | main | Standing_Evaluator2 label | column name says evaluator 2; label repeats evaluator 1 | column name followed; label left as deposited |
| F3 | main | Readme variable list incomplete | ID, ChronicNeckPain and VAS_neck_0to100 not listed; four CVA columns (evaluator by position) covered only by one entry 'CVA (grades)' | columns interpreted from names, SPSS labels and value labels; documented in t01 |
| F4 | main | ID gaps | 92 unique IDs from 1 to 103; 11 numbers absent (16, 58, 60, 61, 63, 66, 67, 68, 69, 84, 102) | ID treated as a study code only; reasons for gaps unknown, not inferred |
| F5 | minor | Angle name | same four columns | read as CVA, as in the readme and record title |
| F6 | minor | Readme citation line | Zenodo and DataCite list two creators | official two creator citation used; co-investigator credited as contributor |
| F7 | minor | NDI scale | NDI values 2 to 40, all even | analysed as deposited on the stated 0 to 100 scale; even values are consistent with a doubled score (inferred, not stated) |
| F8 | minor | CVA resolution | every CVA value is a multiple of 1/3 degree | consistent with each value being a mean of three readings (inferred, not stated); agreement results refer to the deposited values |

**Height unit check (one line):** with Height read as metres, weight / height^2 reproduces the deposited BMI exactly (max absolute difference 0.0e+00); read as cm, as the SPSS label says, BMI would range 177,557 to 408,163, which is impossible. The cm reading is not used in any analysis.

Cross checks between columns (observations, not errors), `tables/t03_consistency_checks.csv`:

| check | rows_flagged | rows_checked |
|-|-|-|
| IPAQ_categorized agrees with IPAQ_total thresholds | 0 | 78 |
| chronic neck pain rows with no neck pain in the last year (NMQ) | 1 | 50 |
| asymptomatic rows with neck pain in the last year (NMQ) | 4 | 42 |
| asymptomatic rows with VAS above 0 | 4 | 42 |
| chronic neck pain rows with VAS equal to 0 | 4 | 50 |
| duplicate IDs | 0 | 92 |

Questionnaire and screening question wording from the SPSS labels is not reproduced. Only the deposited scores are analysed, as they appear in the table.

## 3. Missingness

* NDI_total: present in 48 rows. Missing in all 42 asymptomatic rows and in 2 of 50 chronic neck pain rows. NDI was therefore available only for the pain group, so it cannot be compared between groups.
* IPAQ_total and IPAQ_categorized: missing in 14 rows (7 asymptomatic, 7 chronic neck pain), in the same rows for both columns. IPAQ is described but not used as a covariate.
* VAS: no missing values. The other 16 columns are complete.
* The deposit does not explain the missing values. No imputation is done; analyses are complete case.

| column | missing_asymptomatic_of_42 | missing_chronic_neck_pain_of_50 | missing_total_of_92 |
|-|-|-|-|
| NDI_total | 42 | 2 | 44 |
| IPAQ_total | 7 | 7 | 14 |
| IPAQ_categorized | 7 | 7 | 14 |

## 5. Pre-specified CVA contrasts: chronic neck pain minus asymptomatic

Fixed before computing: OLS with HC3 robust standard errors, 95% CIs, Holm correction across the 4 primary models. CVA in degrees; a negative difference means a smaller angle (more forward head) in the pain group. Adjusted models include age (years), sex and BMI. Figure: `figures/fig04_prespecified_contrasts.png`.

| position | CVA | model | difference (95% CI) | p | p Holm |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| sitting | mean of evaluators | unadjusted | -0.03 (-2.25 to 2.19) | 0.981 | 1.000 |
| sitting | mean of evaluators | adjusted age, sex, BMI | 0.29 (-1.82 to 2.39) | 0.789 | 1.000 |
| standing | mean of evaluators | unadjusted | -0.73 (-2.72 to 1.25) | 0.468 | 1.000 |
| standing | mean of evaluators | adjusted age, sex, BMI | -0.41 (-2.17 to 1.36) | 0.652 | 1.000 |

0 of 4 primary contrasts pass Holm at 0.05. All 95% CIs lie within about -2.7 to 2.4 degrees and include 0. No equivalence margin was pre-specified, so this is not a claim that the groups are equivalent; it describes the precision available from 92 rows.

**Sensitivity, single evaluator (outside the primary Holm family; own Holm across these 8):**

| position | CVA | model | difference (95% CI) | p | p Holm (8) |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| sitting | evaluator 1 | unadjusted | -0.05 (-2.31 to 2.22) | 0.966 | 1.000 |
| sitting | evaluator 1 | adjusted age, sex, BMI | 0.29 (-1.76 to 2.35) | 0.779 | 1.000 |
| sitting | evaluator 2 | unadjusted | -0.00 (-2.23 to 2.22) | 0.998 | 1.000 |
| sitting | evaluator 2 | adjusted age, sex, BMI | 0.28 (-1.92 to 2.48) | 0.803 | 1.000 |
| standing | evaluator 1 | unadjusted | -0.87 (-2.85 to 1.12) | 0.392 | 1.000 |
| standing | evaluator 1 | adjusted age, sex, BMI | -0.55 (-2.30 to 1.20) | 0.538 | 1.000 |
| standing | evaluator 2 | unadjusted | -0.60 (-2.63 to 1.42) | 0.560 | 1.000 |
| standing | evaluator 2 | adjusted age, sex, BMI | -0.26 (-2.09 to 1.56) | 0.778 | 1.000 |

Using one evaluator instead of the mean moves the point estimates by at most 0.14 degrees; 0 of 8 single evaluator contrasts pass Holm and 0 of 8 reach an uncorrected 0.05.

## 6. CVA, sex and BMI

Mean of evaluators. OLS HC3, 95% CIs. Unadjusted models have one term; the adjusted model contains sex, BMI and age together. These are descriptive associations, outside the primary family, without multiplicity correction. `tables/t10_sex_and_bmi_associations.csv`.

| position | term | model | estimate, degrees (95% CI) | p |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| sitting | woman vs man | unadjusted | -2.83 (-5.11 to -0.55) | 0.015 |
| sitting | BMI per 1 kg/m2 | unadjusted | -0.49 (-0.78 to -0.20) | <0.001 |
| sitting | woman vs man | mutually adjusted with age | -2.43 (-4.69 to -0.17) | 0.035 |
| sitting | BMI per 1 kg/m2 | mutually adjusted with age | -0.55 (-0.85 to -0.25) | <0.001 |
| standing | woman vs man | unadjusted | -2.19 (-4.11 to -0.28) | 0.025 |
| standing | BMI per 1 kg/m2 | unadjusted | -0.56 (-0.80 to -0.33) | <0.001 |
| standing | woman vs man | mutually adjusted with age | -2.09 (-4.02 to -0.15) | 0.034 |
| standing | BMI per 1 kg/m2 | mutually adjusted with age | -0.58 (-0.83 to -0.34) | <0.001 |

Women and participants with higher BMI have smaller angles in this table. Neither association says anything about cause. A measurement explanation (landmarks may be harder to place with more soft tissue) cannot be tested without the photographs, which are not in the deposit.

## 8. Sitting versus standing

Mean of evaluators, n 92: Pearson r 0.827 (0.749 to 0.882), Spearman rho 0.820 (0.725 to 0.885). Standing minus sitting: 0.96 degrees (0.34 to 1.57). The two positions rank people similarly but are not interchangeable.

## 9. Agreement of the two deposited evaluator columns

Model: ICC(A,1): two way random effects, absolute agreement, single measure (McGraw and Wong 1996; Shrout and Fleiss ICC(2,1)), McGraw and Wong F based 95% CI. Bland Altman: evaluator 2 minus evaluator 1, 95% limits of agreement with approximate CIs. Computed only from the deposited columns. Each deposited value appears to be a mean of three readings (flag F8, inferred), so these numbers describe agreement of evaluator level values, not of single readings, and they do not reconstruct the paper's reliability protocol. `tables/t12_evaluator_agreement.csv`, `figures/fig05_evaluator_agreement.png`.

| position | ICC(A,1) (95% CI) | ICC(C,1) | bias (95% CI) | limits of agreement | within 1 degree | within 2 degrees | max abs diff |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| sitting | 0.958 (0.933 to 0.974) | 0.962 | 0.49 (0.18 to 0.79) | -2.39 to 3.36 | 68.5% | 91.3% | 8.00 |
| standing | 0.966 (0.949 to 0.977) | 0.966 | 0.08 (-0.18 to 0.34) | -2.36 to 2.52 | 80.4% | 96.7% | 5.67 |

Agreement is high in both positions. In sitting, evaluator 2 reads on average 0.49 degrees higher (paired t p 0.002); the limits of agreement are about plus or minus 3 degrees, wider than the group differences estimated in section 5.

## 10. Limitations

* One small cross sectional sample of young adults from one university; not representative of older or clinical populations.
* Group membership in the table is one yes or no column (ChronicNeckPain) whose SPSS label is a screening question; inclusion criteria are as reported in the paper. A few rows disagree with the NMQ items (section 2).
* Codebook mismatches are resolved by stated assumptions (height in metres, Standing_Evaluator2 is evaluator 2, the four angle columns are CVA). They are flagged, not proven.
* NDI exists only in the pain group and IPAQ is missing in 14 rows; reasons are not documented.
* CVA comes from photographs that are not in the deposit, so landmarking cannot be checked.
* The adjustment set (age, sex, BMI) was fixed in advance but is small; residual confounding is possible. No equivalence margin was set, so null contrasts are not evidence of no difference.
* Nothing here is clinical advice or a diagnostic cutoff.
